channel.title: Sweet Escape Blog
channel.description: Frozen-dessert guides and shop updates from Sweet Escape in Memphis, Tennessee.

item.title: Spaghetti Ice Cream Is Real—But It Isn’t Pasta
item.description: Discover the Mannheim story behind spaghetti ice cream, how its sweet ingredients imitate pasta, and what food-presentation studies can—and cannot—tell us.

item.title: Coffee Beans Are Seeds Inside a Fruit
item.description: Coffee beans begin inside a coffee cherry. Follow the seeds through fruit layers, processing and roasting, with a Sweet Escape coffee-gelato connection.

item.title: A Milkshake Helped Inspire the Bendy Straw
item.description: A milkshake helped inspire the bendy straw. Explore Friedman’s paper prototype, its clever ridges, later redesigns, and the physics behind an ordinary sip.

item.title: The Nobel Banquet Really Had an Ice-Cream Parade
item.description: Explore the Nobel Banquet’s ice-cream procession, illuminated sculptures, changing dessert menus, and a sweet connection to everyday celebrations in Memphis.

item.title: Ice Cream in Bread? A Global Dessert Fun Fact
item.description: Discover Singapore’s bread-wrapped ice cream, Sicily’s gelato-filled brioche, and the surprising variety behind the ice-cream sandwich.

item.title: Why Does Popping Candy Pop? A Dessert Science Fact
item.description: Explore the gas pockets inside popping candy, why ice cream creates a moisture challenge, and how scientists measure a sweet crackle.

item.title: Maple Syrup Starts as Clear Sap—Not Brown Syrup
item.description: Discover how watery maple sap becomes syrup through seasonal weather, concentration and heat, with a Sweet Escape butter-pecan gelato connection.

item.title: Why Does Turkish Ice Cream Stretch?
item.description: Explore the salep and orchid connection behind stretchy Maraş-style ice cream, what elasticity means, and why stretch does not make a dessert melt-proof.

item.title: Pineapple’s Strange Dessert Trick: Why Gelatin Won’t Set
item.description: Discover why fresh pineapple can keep gelatin runny, why canned fruit behaves differently, and how the enzyme mystery connects to a Sweet Escape scoop.

item.title: Did People Really Make Parmesan Ice Cream?
item.description: Parmesan ice cream appears in a 1789 cookbook. Explore its sweetened base, historical iced-cheese names, and a Sweet Escape cheesecake-gelato connection.

item.title: Peanuts Grow Underground—But They Aren’t Roots
item.description: Peanuts start with flowers above the soil, then develop pods underground. Explore pegs, seeds, shells, and the peanut-butter ice-cream connection.

item.title: How Can Ice Cream Survive in a Hot Oven?
item.description: Baked Alaska can keep ice cream frozen while its outside browns. Explore the air pockets, heat transfer, and timing behind this surprising dessert.

item.title: Why Is Dry Ice “Dry”? A Strange Frozen Fact
item.description: Dry ice seems to smoke, yet leaves no meltwater. Learn why frozen carbon dioxide skips the liquid stage—and what the fog really is.

item.title: Can Music Change How Ice Cream Tastes?
item.description: Explore real ice-cream experiments on music, sweetness and flavor, plus a simple listening-and-tasting comparison to try from Sweet Escape Memphis.

item.title: The Navy’s Concrete Ice-Cream Barge Was Real
item.description: Discover the real 1945 floating ice-cream plant, how concrete barges floated, and why producing, storing and delivering frozen dessert were different jobs.

item.title: Why Do Banana Slices Turn Brown?
item.description: Explore the enzyme science behind banana slices turning brown, what can slow the change, and the connection to Sweet Escape’s Banana ice-cream listing.

item.title: Why Do Some Ice Cream Scoops Have a Trigger?
item.description: Explore Alfred Cralle’s one-handed disher, earlier rotating scrapers, and trigger-free dippers in a practical ice-cream design story from Sweet Escape Memphis.

item.title: Why Does Ice Cream Make Soda Foam? A Sweet Escape Fun Fact
item.description: Explore dissolved carbon dioxide, bubble nucleation, and changing foam in an ice-cream soda, with a Sweet Escape dessert-science connection in Memphis.

item.title: Is Cinnamon Really Tree Bark? A Sweet Escape Fun Fact
item.description: Follow cinnamon from a tropical tree to layered spice quills, explore its aroma, and find a verified cinnamon connection at Sweet Escape Memphis.

item.title: Why Does Cotton Candy Seem to Disappear? A Sweet Escape Fun Fact
item.description: Discover the sugar-glass and dissolving science behind cotton candy, plus what the Cotton Candy Twist ice-cream name does—and does not—tell you.
